Same label and year read from both editions: 1933 pairs in state/edition_conflicts.csv sit at a median of exactly 100.00x; the publisher's own world-total implied yield moves from 0.93 to 92 t/ha at 1934. Tobacco AREA is not scaled: all 18 same-year sibling cells agree at 1.00x. Same unit change as tobacco, in the same two late volumes (data_errors.csv iia-hops-x100): 1933 pairs 15 of 15 at 100x. Siblings, same polity: all 17 same-year juan cells are ~100x below the printed value; 16 of 17 land within 2x after division. The 17th, czech republic 1944, prints 46,100 where juan's 3,461 implies 346,100 -- a dropped leading digit on top of the unit, wrong either way and closer after division (7.5x low against 13.3x high). fao1952 1934-1938: 2 of 2 joinable polities within 2x of the divided mean.

iia_1938_39 prints hops AREA in a unit 10x smaller, rounded to 1,000 of it: 1933 pairs 14 of 16 at 10x (data_errors.csv iia-hops-x100). Siblings: czech republic and serbia 1934-1938 are exactly 10x juan on all 10 cells. iia_1939_45 does NOT carry it, which is why the rule stops at 1938: its 1939-1945 hops area equals juan exactly on all 8 cells (czech republic 1939-1945, serbia 1939), and australia (500 ha) and new zealand (200 ha) read on the divided 1934-1937 level. Period averages are not scaled either: the 1934-1938 average is within 2x of fao1952's on all 9 joinable polities, equal on 8. Cells printed as 1,000 for under ~100 ha (the volume's rounding floor) stay approximate after division.
